q1: SELECT f1.drinker, f2.drinker FROM (SELECT drinker, SUM(times_a_week) AS st FROM frequents GROUP BY drinker) AS f1, (SELECT drinker, SUM(times_a_week) AS st FROM frequents GROUP BY drinker) AS f2 WHERE f1.drinker < f2.drinker AND f1.st = f2.st
q2: SELECT f1.drinker, f2.drinker FROM frequents AS f1, frequents AS f2 GROUP BY f1.drinker, f2.drinker HAVING SUM(f1.times_a_week) < SUM(f2.times_a_week)

q2_prompt_sql: SELECT f1.drinker, f2.drinker FROM frequents AS f1, frequents AS f2 GROUP BY f1.drinker, f2.drinker HAVING SUM(f1.times_a_week) < SUM(f2.times_a_week)
explanation: Q1 compares the sum of times_a_week for two drinkers and returns pairs where the sums are equal and the first drinker's name is lexicographically smaller. Q2, due to the cross join and aggregation over all pairs, compares products of sums and counts of bars, leading to different results when sums are equal but bar counts differ.
